standard.title: Construct works for specific audiences
standard.description: use media languages, media technologies and production processes to construct media arts works that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning for specific audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can construct representations using media languages and production processes, communicating ideas and perspectives. They have applied shot types, sound, sequencing and pre-production planning. They have not yet designed works specifically for audiences — applying genre codes and conventions deliberately, or using chroma key, special effects and more advanced editing.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use media languages, media technologies and production processes to construct media arts works that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning for specific audiences.

nodes.label: Audience and genre
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the relationship between audience, purpose and genre — explaining how codes and conventions of an established genre serve specific audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the genre of one media arts work, name two codes or conventions that define it, and explain how those conventions serve the intended audience.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse genre codes and conventions across two or more media forms (genre film, music video, advertisement, game design); explain how conventions create audience expectations and relationships; identify story structures and technical/symbolic elements that contribute to genre formation.
wider: Identify the genre conventions of a music video and explain how they structure the audience experience differently from a narrative film — applying findings to original genre analysis or production planning

Analyse game genre conventions (character design, level design, dialogue conventions) and investigate how each convention builds a specific audience relationship — applying analysis to original character or level design
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding the audience-genre relationship is the prerequisite for all subsequent production decisions — without it, production choices serve personal preference rather than communicative intent for a specific audience.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions to build the reasoning chain: 'How can I adapt and manipulate story principles to make my intention clear for this audience?' Students need explicit practice connecting genre conventions to audience expectation.

success_criteria: Student can identify the genre of a media arts work and name at least two defining codes or conventions
Student can explain how those conventions serve the intended audience

nodes.label: Production planning for audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a media arts production using pre-production tools — designing for a specific audience and making pre-production decisions that serve that audience relationship.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a storyboard or shot list for a key scene in a planned media arts work — including at least two audience-directed decisions (e.g. camera angle choice, sound choice) with written justifications.
nodes.typical_width: Design using pre-production tools (storyboard, shot list, game design plan, script) for specific audiences; apply genre conventions to planning decisions; reflect on the storyboard using Viewpoints questions ('What is working well?', 'What do I need to improve?'); plan permissions and documentation requirements.
wider: Design a storyboard for a short genre film — including camera angles, transitions, edits, voice and soundtrack decisions — and evaluate the storyboard against the intended audience relationship before producing

Design a game character for a specific genre — considering costume, mannerisms, cultural background and typical dialogue for the target audience — and justify each design decision in terms of genre conventions

response_modes.reason: Pre-production planning is a discipline habit that requires practice — students who skip or rush storyboarding produce works that drift from their communicative intent. Invest in thorough planning cycles, not just capture.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of pre-production tools available at Y5-6 (storyboard, shot list, game design plan, script, navigational plan) is genuinely diverse — students who work across multiple planning forms develop much stronger production decision-making.
success_criteria: Student produces a pre-production plan (storyboard, shot list, or equivalent) for a media arts work
Student can explain at least two audience-directed decisions in the plan

nodes.label: Constructing for specific audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a media arts work using advanced production techniques — applying genre conventions and reflecting on whether the work communicates its intended meaning to the specific audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one media arts work for a specific audience, applying at least two genre conventions deliberately, and reflect on how successfully the work communicates to that audience.
nodes.typical_width: Produce media arts works across two or more genres and forms (genre short film, advertisement, game design, music video section) using chroma key, special effects, editing, sound effects and film language; apply genre conventions deliberately; reflect using Viewpoints questions on whether production choices serve the audience.
wider: Create a short genre film using chroma key, special effects, editing, sound effects and film language — applying all five elements deliberately and evaluating how each serves the intended genre audience

Create a section of a music video that brings together music, dance and media arts — considering how the codes and conventions of music videos structure the audience experience, and reflecting on what was successfully communicated

response_modes.reason: Construction for specific audiences integrates genre knowledge, pre-production planning and production skills — the produced work should be evaluated against the intended audience relationship, not just as an object.

success_criteria: Student produces a media arts work for a specific audience applying at least two genre conventions deliberately
Student can explain whether and how the work successfully communicates its intended meaning to that audience
